title: Sociocultural Considerations in Monitoring Anti-LGBTQ+ Content on Social Media
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the detection of anti-LGBTQ+ hate speech that contains religious terms or is framed within a religious context. Specifically, it analyzed whether a model (LTEDI) identified hate speech through religious word-tokens like 'bible', 'god', and 'Adam', which are linked to the Abrahamic creation myth and puritanical beliefs on morality.
findings: The study found that one of the hate speech detection models (LTEDI) identified anti-LGBTQ+ content associated with religious terms (e.g., 'bible', 'god', 'Adam') rather than explicit slurs. This suggests that some anti-LGBTQ+ discourse is framed using religious language, potentially rooted in puritanical moral beliefs. The paper notes that the religious subtext in this model's training data may reinforce polarizing beliefs that religion is inherently anti-LGBTQ+ and raises questions about whether the detected content is primarily hate speech, religious in nature, or both.
